summary: The CLI half is close to implementable apart from a few internal contradictions (kb init/new, kyyn/kyyn-v2, ApiOrigin), but the MCP/Web half is not: its biggest gap is the undefined MCP contract (tool granularity, JSON value encoding and outcome/error mapping).

questions.text: How does secret set receive the value without a mandatory prompt, and does secret show reveal it?
questions.reason: Decides input channel, redaction and result type; ADR only lists the commands, 'checkout-local secrets' and 'no mandatory interactive prompts'.

questions.text: Should ApiOrigin gain a PluginOrigin constructor, or are vendored plugin modules reported under an existing origin?
questions.reason: Fixes the shared data type and JSON origin values; prose demands sdk/generated/kb/plugin origins but the type has only SdkOrigin | GeneratedOrigin | KbOrigin.

questions.text: How does InspectRootApi return the fixed catalogue together with guest.bindings-unavailable diagnostics when its result is Either [Diagnostic] [ApiEntry]?
questions.reason: Decides the effect signature and where degraded-listing logic lives; the ADR requires the partial list plus diagnostics but the declared Either cannot carry both.

questions.text: Does MCP expose each KB tool/plugin method as its own generated MCP tool, or a fixed set of typed discover/invoke tools?
questions.reason: Decides a dynamic vs static tool list (listChanged, naming) and how selective discovery works; ADR only says 'named typed methods and selective discovery', not one command-string tool.

questions.text: Is the KB creation command kb init or kb new (one command or two)?
questions.reason: Sets parser name, help and the not-a-KB hint; hierarchy and init paragraph say kb init, KB selection says 'Explicit kb new owns creation'.

questions.text: What canonical JSON encoding maps Dhall/Haskell contract values (unions, optionals, naturals, extra fields) to MCP/Web inputs, schemas and results, and who decodes it?
questions.reason: Needed for 'same request via CLI/MCP/web, same result'; ADR says generated JSON Schema and structural JSON but never defines the mapping.

questions.text: What mechanism protects the local Web/MCP control surface from unrelated origins (Host/Origin checks, per-launch token, socket)?
questions.reason: Security guarantee shaping middleware and client launch; ADR only says 'Bind locally and protect the control surface from unrelated web origins'.

questions.text: Do MCP/Web responses reuse the CLI outcome/result/diagnostics envelope, and is a refusal an isError result, a protocol error or a successful call?
questions.reason: Failure semantics and output schemas for agents; the envelope and exit table are defined for the CLI adapter only.

questions.text: Where in the JSON envelope do the response kind and selected revision/evolution go, and is the structured output versioned?
questions.reason: Stable structured output scripts depend on; ADR says responses 'identify their kind and selected revision/evolution' but the only envelope shown has outcome/result/diagnostics.

questions.text: Which commands resolve Git identity and refuse when it is missing: only committing ones, or every KB-scoped mutation?
questions.reason: Decides which effect rows include readUserIdentity; ADR says missing identity is refused 'before compilation or mutation' without listing commands.

questions.text: What does kb show return, as distinct from root show?
questions.reason: Decides result type and whether it works on a broken root; it appears only in the hierarchy, which forbids placeholder handlers.

questions.text: What does doctor check, does it need a KB, and do report commands (doctor, root check) signal findings as success or refusal?
questions.reason: Decides its interpreters and exit code on findings; ADR only says 'doctor is a standalone readiness command' and root check 'returns the check report'.

questions.text: Is the installed executable named kyyn or kyyn-v2?
questions.reason: User-facing program name, help and printed recovery commands; the ADR uses both 'kyyn <noun-path> <verb>' and 'kyyn-v2 --kb PATH ...'.

questions.text: What does root recipe run produce, and where does its effect land (new evolution, existing workspace, or recipe state directly)?
questions.reason: Decides whether it needs EvolutionStore/acceptance, identity and the check exit table; ADR says only that closed flows take a request via run and defers state to ADR 0014.

questions.text: What happens when CLI and server requests mutate the same KB or evolution workspace concurrently?
questions.reason: Atomicity of saved candidates and accept; ADR only notes the kernel checks for a branch change between selection and publication.

questions.text: Is a Web/MCP server bound to one KB at start, or does each request carry a KnowledgeBaseRef resolved per call?
questions.reason: Decides request shapes and server resolution/caching; the example request carries knowledgeBase while ADR 0025 is cited for per-KB lifecycles.

questions.text: In a long-running server, are interpreters composed per request or built once per capability and selected per operation?
questions.reason: Shapes server architecture and start-up cost; ADR forbids a kitchen-sink or lazily initialized global runtime but says nothing about server lifetime.

questions.text: How does plugin connector login obtain interactive credentials given no mandatory prompts (device code, browser loopback)?
questions.reason: Decides adapter flow and MCP/Web exposure; login appears only in the hierarchy.

questions.text: What does kb init do when PATH is outside any Git repository or already exists, non-empty or already a KB?
questions.reason: Decides whether init runs git init and which refusals exist; ADR says only that PATH may not exist yet and defers ordering to ADR 0012.

questions.text: Which evolution states (open, ready, accepted, archived) may --evolution select for discovery and browsing?
questions.reason: Decides whether archived target source is readable and the refusal codes; ADR says only that --evolution selects that workspace's target source.

questions.text: Is an invalid --input/--options Dhall value a domain refusal (exit 1) or invalid CLI usage (exit 2)?
questions.reason: Places decoding in the parser or the adapter; ADR says a type mismatch keeps the normal Dhall diagnostic and decodes against the inspected contract, without naming the exit.

questions.text: How are root query execute and root output preview results rendered, and do they accept --evolution?
questions.reason: Dhall-default/JSON convention is stated for tools and connector methods only; the hierarchy shows no --evolution for queries or outputs.

questions.text: Does guest discovery with a non-KB --kb (explicit or default '.') fall back to catalogue-only or refuse?
questions.reason: Needs a special case in shared KB resolution; 'outside a KB, discovery reads only the catalogue' conflicts with 'not a KB returns an actionable error'.

questions.text: How is evolution new --before COMMIT validated (full ID only, ancestor of HEAD, contains this KB)?
questions.reason: ADR allows an explicit full commit ID (hierarchy lists containment, not every argument) but gives no validation or refusal rules.

questions.text: With --json, does a usage error (exit 2) also emit a JSON envelope on stdout?
questions.reason: Scripts need to know whether every invocation yields an envelope; ADR keeps optparse's standard help/usage presentation but does not say whether an envelope accompanies it.
